draft.title: Venn diagrams and set notation
card: A ∪ B means in A, or in B, or in both. On a Venn diagram it is everything inside either circle.
A ∩ B means in both A and B. On a Venn diagram it is the overlap of the two circles.
A′ means not in A. On a Venn diagram it is everything outside the circle for A.
Adding P(A) and P(B) counts the overlap twice, so subtract it once: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B). Example: P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.4 and P(A ∩ B) = 0.2 give P(A ∪ B) = 0.5 + 0.4 − 0.2 = 0.7.
draft.remember: Union is either or both. Subtract the overlap once so it is not counted twice.

a.q: In a Year 11 class, P(A) = 0.6, P(B) = 0.3 and P(A ∩ B) = 0.1. What is P(A ∪ B)?
a.why: P(A ∪ B) = 0.6 + 0.3 − 0.1 = 0.8. The answer 0.9 comes from adding without subtracting the overlap, which counts the overlap twice.

b.q: At a school, 40% of students play netball (N) and 25% play tennis (T). 10% play both. What is the probability a student plays neither sport?
b.why: P(N ∪ T) = 0.40 + 0.25 − 0.10 = 0.55. Neither is the complement of the union, so 1 − 0.55 = 0.45. The answer 0.55 is wrong because it is the probability of playing at least one sport.
b.clue: Find the union first, then take its complement.
